/-!
# Erdős Problem 172

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/172](https://www.erdosproblems.com/172)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos172

/--
Is it true that in any finite colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there exist arbitrarily large finite $A$ such that all sums
and products of distinct elements in $A$ are the same colour?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_172 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (color : ℕ → Fin n) (m), ∃ (A : Finset ℕ), A.card ≥ m ∧ ∃ c, ∀ (S : Finset A),
    S.Nonempty → color (∑ x ∈ S, x) = c ∧ color (∏ x ∈ S, x) = c := by
  sorry

-- TODO: add the statements from the additional material
end Erdos172

reformulations.difference: Lean permits 0 in the generating set A, unlike the positive-integer convention used in the arithmetic Ramsey literature.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The monochromatic nonempty-subset sums/products condition is inherited by subsets. For a desired size m, take a Lean witness of size at least m+1 and delete 0; the resulting positive set still has size at least m and satisfies the same condition. Conversely, positive witnesses are also natural-number witnesses. Colorings of the positive integers can be extended arbitrarily to 0, and colorings of Lean's naturals can be restricted to the positives. A full quantifier-level equivalence with the positive-generator formulation was proved in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean without using the conjecture.

review.notes: The file contains only one problem declaration. Its quantifiers, common color, distinct-element encoding, nonempty-subset restriction, and answer-slot scope agree with the finite sums/products conjecture in the accessible literature. Scratch Lean proofs verify the equivalence of Finset A with explicit finite subsets of A, the harmless inclusion of zero, and the equivalence of cardinality bounds with exact sizes. Boundary tests cover zero colors, one color, sizes 0 and 1, empty operations, and small nonconstant colorings. Alweiss's July 2026 version still describes the natural-number conjecture as open, and the independent database lists #172 as open. No mathematical defect or status discrepancy was established.
